title: Experiment Slicing Field Notes and Fallback Protocols (WIP)
content:
Purpose and context:

Quick working notes for an operational pattern that combines small canaries, phased A/B experiments, and an automated fallback surface that sites on routing/console. Goal is to reduce blast radius while giving product and SRE teams predictable guardrails. This is deliberately rough — capturing heuristics we tried in Feb and questions to resolve before formalizing as a playbook.

Overview (one-liner):
- Slice traffic by orthogonal signals (region, plan tier, request type) -> run overlapping canaries -> promote via metric gates -> automatic fallback if composite risk threshold breached.

Why this felt necessary (field observations):
- Single-signal canaries (by user id) masked regressions that only showed up in high-seq-length requests.
- Sudden latency spikes surfaced in a burst scenario (hourly ad-hoc jobs) even though percentile SLOs looked fine for small samples.
- Rollbacks were slow because ownership handoffs were unclear; automation should collapse manual cognitive load.

Heuristic: orthogonal slicing + weighted gating
- Primary slice axes (ordered): request-sequence-length-bin, plan-tier (free/paid/enterprise), region, route-type (chat/generate/embed).
- For an initial canary: choose 2 axes and run at 1% global traffic but 10% within chosen slice. Example: sequence-long requests on paid tier in us-west -> 1% global, 10% of that slice.
- Rationale: ensures risk concentrated where higher cost/impact lives while keeping overall exposure low.

Metric gates (must be adaptable per rollout):
- Latency: p95 and p99 token generation time compared to baseline; gate if p99 > baseline_p99 * 1.25 for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Error rate: user-visible failures per 1k reqs. Gate if > baseline + 0.5% absolute or 2x relative, whichever is smaller.
- Quality proxy: rate of prompt-regeneration or immediate retry within 30s; gate if > baseline + 1%.
- Cost signal: tokens per request delta; gate if > 15% increase and sustained 1h.
- Composite risk score: normalized combination of the above (weighed: latency 0.35, errors 0.35, quality 0.2, cost 0.1). If composite > 0.6 for 10m -> auto-fallback.

Fallback surface (automation options):
- Model variant swap: instant switch to a pinned stable model variant in the same family (fast).
- Region fallback: route impacted slices to other region cluster with spare capacity.
- Throttle/breaker: reduce tokens-per-request cap for affected slice temporarily.
- Conservative default: canary abort then gradual step-down to 0% for that slice, with notify-on-abort.

Operational play (step-by-step rough):
1) Pre-launch checklist (owners: PM, Eng, SRE):
   - Confirm slice axes and rationale (doc this).
   - Baseline window: choose 48h of production traffic baseline for the same slice axes.
   - Define metric thresholds and expected variance.
   - Hooks: Slack channel, on-call list, and automated PagerDuty escalation rule.
   - Linked rollout ticket and PRs in the lineup.
2) Start canary (SRE triggers):
   - Deploy variant to canary pool; enable routing rule for slice at 1% global (or smaller if very risky).
   - Enable metric collection with 30s granularity for latency/error and 5m for quality proxies.
3) Observe-phase (first 30 min):
   - 1st checkpoint at 5m: sanity check (errors < 0.5% of slice).
   - 2nd checkpoint at 30m: run A/B stats for quality proxies, check composite score.
   - If safe: scale to 5% (or 20% within slice) and continue.
4) Promotion-phase:
   - Promotion windows bounded to business hours or defined maintenance windows for riskier rollouts.
   - Use progressive doubling (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%) with 30–60m observation between steps.
5) Abort/rollback:
   - Auto-fallback triggers if composite > threshold.
   - On abort: run immediate notify (Slack/PagerDuty), create rollback ticket with tags, and kick off postmortem capture template.

Open questions & trade-offs (notes to resolve before doc lock):
- How do we weight user-visible quality vs server-side errors for enterprise customers vs free tier? (Suggestion: separate gating weights by tier; enterprise gets stricter quality gates).
- Do we allow overlapping canaries for the same physical model across slices? Current prototype allows overlap but makes attribution hard. Consider exclusive buckets per model rollout.
- Sampling windows: is 48h baseline always enough for low-traffic slices? Maybe need synthetic load tests for rare slices.
- Alert fatigue: auto-fallback creates noise if thresholds too tight; need runbook-level hysteresis and human-in-the-loop for non-critical noisepoints.

Quick checklists (copyable):
- Pre-launch: [ ] Baseline captured, [ ] Thresholds set, [ ] Runbook channel ready, [ ] Oncall assigned, [ ] QA smoke tests OK
- During rollout: [ ] 5m check, [ ] 30m statistics, [ ] compare composite to baseline, [ ] document anomalies in ticket
- Post-abort: [ ] postmortem template filled within 48h, [ ] follow-up action assigned, [ ] metrics replay attached

Minimal monitoring config snippet (concept):
- metrics: [latency_p95_slice, latency_p99_slice, request_error_rate_slice, regen_rate_slice, tokens_per_req_slice]
- alert_rules:
   - name: "canary-composite-high"
     window: "10m"
     condition: "composite_score > 0.6"
     action: ["fallback:variant-swap", "notify:#rollouts-notify", "pd:severity-3"]

Notes from Feb experiment (what happened):
- Experiment: small model param change rolled to paid tier, region=eu-central, sequence-long slice.
- Result: transient p99 spike at t+18m caused composite breach; automation swapped variant successfully but the subsequent redistribution created a small surge in tokens-per-req; we need guard for transient after-swap metric blips.
- Lesson: add 3m cool-down after automated variant swap before taking further autoscaling actions.

Suggested next steps:
- Iterate on composite scoring function with offline replay of Feb logs. Owner: Owen. Deadline: 2025-03-09.
- Draft console UI mock for slice definition (allow teams to pick axes and preview estimated exposure). Owner: Lina. Deadline: 2025-03-16.
- Small experiment: reserve exclusive canary buckets for 2 upcoming small launches and compare attribution quality. Owner: Jordan. Deadline: 2025-03-23.

Appendix (links & snippets):
- Linear ticket: CORE-3142 (linked above) — rollout automation prototype work.
- PR: console routing rule prototype (github PR link above).
- Quick grep commands we used to pull metrics: 
   - `logs query "model_variant=staging AND region=eu-central" --last 48h | jq .p99`

Random ideas shelved for later:
- ML-driven slice suggestion: a small job that suggests risky slice axes based on correlation of anomalies historically (may help for low-traffic edge cases).
- Canary contract: require a minimal smoke test contract (deterministic prompt -> expected token range) for any model variant to be eligible for automated fallback.

Questions for review meeting:
- Are we comfortable with composite gating vs independent gates? Pros/cons?
- What SLA breach tolerances should map to immediate PD pages vs async Slack only?
- Is there appetite to let product owners opt into more aggressive promotion cadence?

--
Notes-style signoff: rough, patched together during pairing sessions with SRE. Intend to turn into a proper playbook once questions above are resolved.
